$comment: SPIR-V 1.6 module format. First SPIR-V schema (plan 14 LK9, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/spirv.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. LK9 ships the linker SKELETON only — the walker emits the 5-word (20-byte) module header per SPIR-V Spec §2.3 (magic 0x07230203 + version 0x00010600 + generator 0 + bound 0 + reserved 0); plan 17 (MIR→SPIR-V) fills the OpCapability / OpExtension / OpMemoryModel / OpEntryPoint / OpTypeFunction / Op* instruction stream. No `sections[]` declared because SPIR-V emits no sections (the entire module after the header is one typed instruction stream); the universal-field reject in the JSON loader (added at LK8 post-fold) enforces this absence. No `relocations[]` because SPIR-V has no traditional native-style relocations — intra-module references are `<id>`s resolved by the GPU driver at module-load time.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO `predefinedMacros` -- `dataModel` above is ILP32, and `__LP64__`/`_LP64` name the LP64 model specifically, so neither may be defined here. The absence is an ANSWER, not an omission, and is pinned as one by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp. (This format is DECLARED-ONLY anyway -- the semantic consumer fails loud when an ILP32 format is actually selected -- so no C program on this leg can observe it yet; the row exists so the file STATES its answer instead of defaulting into one.)
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 32-bit data model (int 32, long 32, ptr 32) -- DECLARED-ONLY: the semantic consumer fails loud (S_UnsupportedDataModel) when an ILP32 format is actually selected, so no untested width path runs. REQUIRED closed-enum field like every format.
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: REQUIRED closed-enum field on EVERY format, including the declared-only skeletons. This format ships no C header surface of its own, so it declares the CONSERVATIVE value: byte-exact matching can only ever REJECT a spelling loudly, never silently ACCEPT one the target would reject. Revisit if/when a real header convention is defined for it.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: SPIR-V has NO C ABI surface at all -- linkage is expressed as `OpDecorate <id> LinkageAttributes` on the module's own typed instructions, and there is no flat C symbol table to decorate. DOCUMENTED (SPIR-V spec, Linkage decorations) and consistent with the tree's own `kCManglingRules` row, `false` for spirv since FF4. DECLARED rather than omitted for the same reason the wasm skeleton declares it: the key is REQUIRED on EVERY format, so `none` is a DECLARED answer and not a silence from which a future file could inherit a scheme. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the RESERVED spelling, meaning this format has NO register-level C calling convention at all — not an unknown one. `resolveAbi` turns it into a NULL cc pointer, which is the signal the driver (D_TargetAbiModelUnsupportedByDriver) and FFI ingest (F_FfiIngestAbiModelUnsupported) already refuse on. Declared rather than OMITTED because omission is indistinguishable from an oversight, and the key is REQUIRED on every format for that reason. `TargetSchemaData::validate()` refuses a callingConventions[] row named `none`, so this spelling can never also denote a real convention.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
